feedback.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=x(t)+y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)={x}^{3}(t)+y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following gives all equilibrium points of the system of differential equations above?
feedback.worked_solution:
The equilibrium (fixed) points of a system ${x}^{′}(t)=f(x,y)$ are the points for which $f(x,y)=0.$ So, we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+y=0 \\ {x}^{3}+y=0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the first equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x+y=0\,⇒\,y=-x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $y$ into the second equation

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}+y & =0 \\ {x}^{3}-x & =0 \\ x({x}^{2}-1) & =0 \\ x & =-1,\text{ }0,\text{ }1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $y:$

- For $x=0,$ we get $y=0.$

- For $x=1,$ we get $y=-1.$

- For $x=-1,$ we get $y=1.$

Therefore, the equilibrium points are

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,\text{and}\,[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
